title: balance.json `health` block parsed with non-strict jint — decimals truncate and out-of-range ints wrap silently
detail: The 4.3 health block is new catalog data yet uses legacy jint: `"drain_cap_pct_per_tick": 2.9` silently becomes 2 and an out-of-i32-range integer silently wraps — contradicting the jint_strict wrap/truncation rationale the same feature's packet_types fields enforce.
recommended_fix: Parse the health block with jint_strict and reject on any ok==false ("sim fields must be integers"), mirroring the packet_types health fields.

title: balance.health.win_uptime_pct is documented as the win threshold but the sim never reads it — win threshold is dual-sourced
detail: win_uptime_pct is load-validated and folded into the catalog hash (shifting every golden) but is referenced nowhere in the sim — win_lose_eval compares against run-setup surge_win_pct. ODN-5 single-source broken; balance.json's threshold cannot affect gameplay.
recommended_fix: Single-source the threshold: either delete balance.health.win_uptime_pct (validation + data + tests) or have win_lose_eval read the catalog value instead of surge_win_pct.

title: Grace_Expired event silently dropped when the expired class's severity is 0 (drain == 0)
detail: Validation permits health_drain_pct_per_tick == 0. If the only post-grace class has severity 0, drain stays 0, the `expired` collection is never emitted, and the arch's `Grace_Expired{class}` event contract (§6.5 interface) never fires for that expiry.
recommended_fix: Emit the collected Grace_Expired events regardless of drain, or tighten validation to require health_drain_pct_per_tick >= 1.
